t: You are at the site of Newgate Prison, which stood at the corner of Newgate Street and Old Bailey. It began at Newgate, a gate in the Roman London Wall. The prison was in use for over 700 years, from 1188 to 1902, and was demolished in 1904. Sir Thomas Malory, author of Le Morte d'Arthur, died here, and he called himself a knight prisoner. The poisoner Thomas Neill Cream was hanged here in 1892. The counterfeiter Catherine Murphy, the last woman in England officially burned at the stake, died here, and so did the child killer Amelia Dyer.
